definitions.explanation: humble way to say that one will go along with someone of higher status

examples.japanese: ⟦{社長|しゃちょう}→社長：01428_shachou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{出張|しゅっちょう}→出張：01094_shucchou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{供|とも}します。
examples.english: I will accompany the president on his business trip.

examples.japanese: ぜひお{供|とも}⟦させて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please allow me to accompany you.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{供|とも}した。
examples.english: I accompanied my teacher on her shopping.

notes:
KEIGO TYPE:
Humble speech (⟦{謙譲語|けんじょうご}→謙譲語：15869_kenjougo⟧). Used when the speaker accompanies someone of higher status.

サ{変|へん} verb (⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ verb)
- お{供|とも}します (polite)
- お{供|とも}⟦させて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦いただきます→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧ (very humble)

RELATED WORDS:
- お{供|とも} - companion; attendant (noun)
- ⟦{同行|どうこう}する→同行する：21427_doukousuru⟧ - to accompany (neutral)
- ⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧ - to go together (casual)

TRADITIONAL CONTEXT:
Historically, お{供|とも} referred to servants or retainers accompanying their lord. Today it's used in business and formal contexts.
